title: Sticky Toffee Pudding with Date Sponge and Toffee Sauce
summary: A moist date sponge soaked in a buttery toffee sauce, served warm with extra sauce and a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
plain flour, plus extra for the tin
unsalted butter, at room temperature, plus extra for the tin
fine sea salt or table salt
scoops vanilla ice cream, to serve

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Cook 450 g dates in 480 ml water for 5 min until soft, then off the heat stir in 2 tsp bicarbonate of soda and ¼ tsp salt, cool 10 min and purée smooth.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk 450 g flour and 2 tsp baking powder together.

steps.title: Cream
steps.text: Beat 140 g butter and 450 g sugar until pale and fluffy, 3-4 min, then beat in 5 eggs one at a time and 2 tsp vanilla.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: On low speed add the flour in three additions, alternating with the date purée, mixing just until combined.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Spread the batter in a buttered and floured tin and bake at 175 °C until risen and a skewer comes out clean, 50-60 min.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.text: Melt 225 g butter, 225 g dark brown sugar and ¼ tsp salt until bubbling, then whisk in 240 ml cream and ½ tsp vanilla and simmer 2-3 min.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Poke the warm cake all over with a skewer and pour over about a third of the sauce, letting it soak in for 10 min.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cut into squares and serve warm with more sauce and a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

tips: Let the bicarbonate of soda foam into the hot date mixture fully before puréeing for a soft, moist crumb.
Add the flour and date purée in alternating additions on low speed to avoid overworking the batter.
Poke the warm sponge all over before pouring over the sauce so it soaks right through.
safety: Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best served warm the day it's made; keep any leftovers covered and reheat gently with a little extra sauce.
